approval.cost: No fee is stated on any page read; the key is repeatedly called a 'Free API Key'
approval.trigger: No approval step is documented for obtaining or using an API key, and none gates the OAuth flow: external users can connect without any Eventbrite review. Review exists only for the optional App Marketplace listing (App Approval Process page): 'After creating your API Key, you can go to Directory Listing tab in App Management', then 'Once your app is ready to be in the Eventbrite App Marketplace, submit it to review by clicking the Submit for Review button. That will change your app's status from Unsaved or Draft to Eventbrite Pending Action.' Post-review statuses: 'Eventbrite pending action' ('Your app submission will be reviewed by Eventbrite'), 'Approved' ('Your app is approved and is now listed in the Eventbrite App Marketplace'), 'Rejected' ('Your app submission wasn't approved'), and 'Developer pending action' ('Your app submission has issues that must be addressed and resubmitted before being approved'); status updates arrive by email. A separate App Extension review (for the product page Install button) has statuses Pending review / Approved / Declined. Caps: no pre-approval usage or connected-user caps are stated; the operative numeric limits are the API rate limits (see Time): default 2,000 calls/hour and 48,000 calls/day per token, with Event Action limits of 200 calls/hour for Create and Copy Event, Publish Event, and Create Event Schedule.
approval.wait: Marketplace review timeline: not stated (no duration appears anywhere on the approval page)

blockers.detail: Refresh tokens are never mentioned anywhere in the docs read (text searches for 'refresh' found no matches on the API reference or the App OAuth Flow page). The documented remedy for an expired token is re-running the flow: 'If the User's OAuth Token expires (which may happen, if for example the User changes their password), you'll receive an error. In this instance, your User must again go through the OAuth Token Flow.' (The docs add that if the user still has confirmed access to your application, they will not be required to do that step again.)
blockers.howToClear: Design for re-authorization as the recovery path; there is no silent refresh to build.
blockers.title: No refresh tokens, and no stated token lifetime

blockers.detail: Scopes are never mentioned anywhere in the docs read, and neither authorize-URL example includes a scope parameter. The grant is a single token tied to the authorizing account/user, with no per-permission selection documented: connecting users cannot grant you a narrower slice.
blockers.howToClear: Treat the token as full-account access: store it carefully and be transparent with users about the access level.
blockers.title: No scopes: one all-or-nothing token

flavor.recommended: An API Key (app) with the server-side authorization code flow
flavor.why: The credential object is an API Key, also called an app; in the OAuth handshake the key is the 'App Key' and is sent as client_id. The docs' 'What You'll Need' list is exactly three items: API Key, Client Secret, Redirect URI, available from the Eventbrite App Management page: the App Key 'Identifies your app during the OAuth handshake. Not secret.', the Client Secret 'Identifies your app during a server-side handshake. Secret.', and the Redirect URI 'You need to set this in the Eventbrite app settings.' Creating one starts with a free Eventbrite account: 'Go to the Developer Portal and click Get a Free API Key'. The key also yields a private token for the owner's own account. For third-party users, the reference documents two authorize variants and states: 'There are two ways to authorize users: Server-side and client-side. We strongly recommend handling authorization on the server side for security reasons.' The server-side exchange returns the user's private token in the JSON response: 'Use this private token to make API requests on behalf of this user.'

humanMust: In the Developer Portal click 'Get a Free API Key'; for an app integration, note the App Key and Client Secret on the Eventbrite App Management page and set the Redirect URI in the Eventbrite app settings
(Optional, Marketplace only) Fill in the Directory Listing tab in App Management and click 'Submit for Review'
name: Eventbrite
nuances: Calls authenticate with the header Authorization: Bearer MYTOKEN or the query parameter ?token=MYTOKEN, against the base URL eventbriteapi.com/v3, with the flow repeated per user: 'For every user you would like to perform API requests on behalf of, repeat Authorize your Users and Authenticate API Requests.'
The documented authorize example uses http://localhost:8080/oauth/redirect?code=YOUR_ACCESS_CODE, so localhost redirect URIs are part of the documented development flow.
Rate-limit errors are explicit: 429 HIT_RATE_LIMIT, 'Hourly rate limit has been reached for this token. Default rate limits are 2,000 calls per hour.'
prerequisites: A Redirect URI set in the Eventbrite app settings

steps.detail: Create a free Eventbrite account, then in the Developer Portal click 'Get a Free API Key'. For an app integration, open the Eventbrite App Management page, note the App Key and Client Secret, and set the Redirect URI in the Eventbrite app settings.
steps.title: Create the account; get the API key; set the redirect URI

steps.detail: Redirect the user to eventbrite.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=YOUR_API_KEY&redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URI. The user approves on Eventbrite's Approve/Deny page, and your redirect URI receives the access code as a query parameter. POST it to eventbrite.com/oauth/token (Content-type application/x-www-form-urlencoded) with grant_type=authorization_code, client_id, client_secret, code, and redirect_uri. The user's private token is returned in the JSON response; store it per user.
steps.title: Run the server-side OAuth flow per user

steps.detail: Call eventbriteapi.com/v3 with Authorization: Bearer <token> (or ?token=<token>). Defaults: 2,000 calls/hour and 48,000 calls/day per token; Create and Copy Event, Publish Event, and Create Event Schedule are each limited to 200 calls/hour.
steps.title: Call the API within the rate limits

steps.detail: Only if you want discovery: fill in the Directory Listing tab in App Management and click 'Submit for Review' (status moves from Unsaved or Draft to Eventbrite Pending Action; outcomes are Approved, Rejected, or Developer pending action, sent by email).
steps.title: (Optional) Submit for Marketplace listing

tagline: The simplest OAuth in the library: a free API key, a two-step server-side flow, no approval gate for connecting users, and no scopes at all. The trade-offs are equally plain: no refresh tokens and no stated token lifetime, so a dead token means the user goes through the flow again.

time.active: ~10 min of account setup + ~30 min of flow code
time.total: Same day (optional Marketplace review duration not stated)
